statementSource.compiledSql:
select "id" from "page_revisions" where ("page_revisions"."created_at" < $1 and (select count(*) from (
        select 1 from "page_revisions" newer
        where newer.page_id = "page_revisions"."page_id"
          and (newer.version, newer.id) > ("page_revisions"."version", "page_revisions"."id")
        limit $2
      ) newer_rows) = $3 and not ("page_revisions"."kind" = 'publish' and not exists (
        select 1 from "page_revisions" published
        where published.page_id = "page_revisions"."page_id"
          and published.kind = 'publish'
          and (published.version, published.id) > ("page_revisions"."version", "page_revisions"."id")
        limit 1))) order by "page_revisions"."created_at" asc, "page_revisions"."id" asc limit $4

knownLimitationHandoff.finding: The whole-family candidate read walks page_revisions_retention_idx in (created_at, id) order and evaluates the correlated keep-newest floor probe (LIMIT keepNewest=100 over the per-parent indexes) for every aged row until 500 candidates match. When most parents hold <= 100 rows (sparse candidates), no row qualifies, so one statement walks the whole aged range with one probe per row: cost ~ aged_rows x min(newer_rows, 100) index entries. The index is used and no Seq Scan appears, but latency scales linearly with the aged range and breaches the 5 s budget / 15 s statement timeout at 100k sparse rows.
proposedMitigation: Bound rows EXAMINED, not only rows returned: read a keyset window over page_revisions_retention_idx (inner ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT <scan window, e.g. 2,000>) and apply the floor/anchor probes to that window only; persist the (created_at, id) high-water mark per family so the next batch/run resumes after it (restart from the beginning once the aged range is exhausted).

Alternatively/additionally semi-join parents that can hold candidates at all (page_id IN (SELECT page_id ... GROUP BY page_id HAVING count(*) > keepNewest), bounded) so sparse parents are skipped without per-row probes.

L03 must treat a statement-timeout cancel of the candidate read as a bounded batch failure (retention_batch_failed) and must not retry-spin; the L01 retention job's tx-local statement_timeout is 4 s (RETENTION_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS), below the 10k-row sparse latency measured here.
